children: The larger project runs through 2031 for railway recruitment services, while the second covers technology and cybersecurity support through 2029

RailTel Corporation of India has secured two work orders worth a combined Rs 186.51 crore, including a Rs 167.52 crore contract from the Railway Recruitment Board (RRB), Secunderabad, for recruitment examination services.

The company received both orders on 16 October, according to its regulatory filing. The contracts cover recruitment examination management as well as IT infrastructure and cybersecurity solutions, further adding to RailTel's project pipeline.

The larger order, estimated at Rs 167.52 crore excluding taxes, covers AM-RMS services for the pre-examination and post-examination stages of RRB recruitment conducted through various Centralised Employment Notifications (CENs).

The contract is scheduled to remain valid until 15 October 2031, giving RailTel a long-term engagement to provide services associated with the recruitment examination process conducted by the railway recruitment board.

The second order, worth Rs 18.99 crore including taxes, has been awarded by Health Insurance TPA of India Ltd for IT infrastructure and cybersecurity solutions. The three-year contract is scheduled to run until 16 October 2029, expanding RailTel's recent project wins across technology, digital infrastructure and cybersecurity-related services.
The latest contracts follow several orders secured by RailTel in recent months, covering digital governance, telecom infrastructure and technology services for government and public-sector clients.

On 13 October, RailTel received a Rs 49 crore order, including taxes, from the Odisha government's Higher Education Department to develop 83 digital application modules under a Comprehensive Digital Governance Platform.
In August, the company secured a Rs 165 crore contract, including taxes, from Western Coalfields to establish a Multiprotocol Label Switching Virtual Private Network on a rental basis for 60 months.

The Western Coalfields contract is scheduled to continue until 20 September 2031. RailTel also received a Rs 166.8 crore order from the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation in August to extend an existing Infrastructure-as-a-Service arrangement through RailTel by one year.
The EPFO contract includes additional components and is scheduled to run until 9 February 2027. RailTel shares closed at Rs 255.05 on the BSE on 16 October, rising 0.57 per cent during the session.
